html:
The Hoti are a small Indigenous people of the forested Guiana Highlands in southern Venezuela, between the Orinoco's tributaries in the states of Bolívar and Amazonas. Their language has no known relatives.

They live by hunting with blowguns and bows, gathering, especially wild honey and palm fruits, and tending small gardens, moving between camps. They stayed largely out of contact with outsiders until the 1960s and 1970s, when missionaries reached them. Neighbours include the Yanomami and the Ye'kuana.
